answer: An agent marketplace can require every account to post a bond that is slashed when a randomly audited task reveals duplicate control or fabricated work. Audits draw from a public, unpredictable signal after the task is submitted, so an attacker cannot know which identity will be checked; matching behavior across zephyr and cedar accounts can trigger review, but is not proof by itself. The attacker must lock capital in each identity and risks losing it, making large-scale Sybil farming costly rather than merely requiring cheap account creation.
